# Queue Safety and Lifecycle Recovery Checklist: Safely Queue Parallel Pull Requests

**Purpose**: Formal implementation-gate review of whether queue-safety, stale-candidate prevention, dependency ordering, and lifecycle-recovery requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable
**Created**: 2026-10-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when a peer PR reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are admission requirements complete for approval, unresolved change requests, current-head checks, labels, open state, same-repository scope, and durable checkpoint evidence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the exact source head, target revision, candidate revision, and eligibility evidence required at each validation and merge decision explicitly documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK003 Are terminal and nonterminal outcomes defined for merge success, stale validation, deterministic incompatibility, transient failure, cancellation, and operator intervention? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Are lifecycle requirements documented for startup, reload, restart, repeated polling, reconciliation, cancellation, closure, approval dismissal, label removal, source update, target movement, merge completion, and partial provider failure? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-011, Constitution III]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is “one pull request at a time” scoped unambiguously to a repository and target-branch queue key, including whether distinct queue keys may advance concurrently? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the stable admission order defined with an objective primary key and tie-breaker, and is the point at which an entry receives that order explicit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “current” eligibility evidence tied unambiguously to the admitted source generation and active candidate revision rather than merely to the pull request number? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Are deterministic incompatibilities distinguished from transient infrastructure failures using criteria that can be applied without subjective judgment? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the recovery action for every blocked or removed outcome stated precisely enough to identify whether the author, operator, or coordinator owns the next step? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-015]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Are queue ordering and explicit dependency ordering consistent when a later-admitted prerequisite must advance before an earlier-admitted dependent entry? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the no-continuous-rebase requirement and the active-head final-integration update requirement consistent across the specification, plan, and merge-queue contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Plan §Phase 0, Contract §Candidate validation]
- [ ] CHK012 Are source-head changes consistently treated as a new generation that invalidates old checks, approvals where policy requires, validation evidence, and admission identity? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the stated GitHub-visible durable authority and the single in-memory coordinator ownership boundary reconciled without creating two competing sources of truth? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Plan §Technical Context]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Can serialized integration be objectively assessed from the acceptance scenarios and success criteria without relying on timing luck or an undefined observation window? [Measurability, Spec §US1, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK015 Can stale-target rejection be objectively assessed by comparing named source, target, and candidate revisions immediately before the merge decision? [Measurability, Spec §US1/AC2, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the idempotency criteria measurable for duplicate admission, repeated polls, restart recovery, and ambiguous merge responses? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-010, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the requirements for permitting an independent successor to advance after a failed head precise enough to distinguish safe advancement from unsafe reordering? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §US2/AC1, Spec §FR-006]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 Are primary, alternate, exception, and recovery requirements present for successful sequential merges, target movement, source movement, conflicts, check failures, and re-entry? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Are partial-failure requirements defined for a lost merge response, successful remote mutation with failed checkpoint write, successful branch update with failed check observation, and restart during validation? [Gap, Recovery]
- [ ] CHK020 Are dependency requirements complete for chains, diamonds, cycles, self-links, duplicates, missing pull requests, cross-repository links, and closed-unmerged prerequisites? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK021 Are cancellation and eligibility-loss requirements specified for every state, including while queued, held, validating, merge-ready, transiently blocked, and update-required? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are concurrent external changes addressed, including an out-of-band target merge, another actor updating the source, and repository policy changing during validation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-010]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK023 Are bounded retry and backoff requirements quantified or explicitly delegated to an existing documented configuration contract? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK024 Are observability requirements complete enough to correlate queue key, pull request, issue, source/target/candidate revisions, outcome, reason, and recovery action without exposing credentials or raw provider payloads? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, Constitution II, Constitution VI]
- [ ] CHK025 Are scale assumptions or supported limits for active repositories, target branches, queued entries, and dependency-graph size documented where they materially affect correctness? [Gap, Scalability]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK026 Are repository approval, required-check, branch-protection, update-branch, and conditional-merge policy dependencies identified with their authoritative evidence and failure semantics? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the assumption that GitHub-visible checkpoints can reconstruct stable admission order and every nonterminal state validated for deletion, duplication, malformed data, and version migration? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK028 Are trust boundaries explicit between issue workers, the queue coordinator, host-authenticated GitHub calls, repository policy, and human merge authority? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Constitution II, Constitution IV]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after peer review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline and link to the relevant artifact when a criterion needs remediation.
